clues.fact: Of an estimated 600 million domestic cats worldwide, 400 million live in Asia, including 58 million in China.

clues.name: Australian Magpie
clues.fact: Australian magpies can recognise at least 100 different people and may be less likely to swoop the ones they've befriended.

clues.name: Little Pied Cormorant
clues.fact: In New Zealand the mostly black, white-throated form wins out, and even in Northland only about one in four birds is pied.

clues.name: Gray Shrikethrush
clues.fact: One of Australasia's best-loved songbirds, it's common over most of Australia but missing from the driest inland deserts.

clues.name: Red-backed Kingfisher
clues.fact: A kingfisher that often lives far from water, it digs its nesting burrow into steep banks above dry creek beds.

clues.name: Eurasian Blackbird
clues.fact: Its name dates from when 'bird' meant a small bird and crows were 'fowl,' making it the only common black 'bird' in the British Isles.

clues.name: Ruddy Turnstone
clues.fact: In every season it wears a harlequin pattern of brown, black and white, set on short, bright orange legs.

clues.name: Green Sea Turtle
clues.fact: The green in its name comes from the fat under its shell, colored by a seagrass diet, while the shell itself is olive to black.

clues.name: Moorish Idol
clues.fact: Some Southeast Asian fishermen release it when caught and bow to it afterward, apparently the source of its name.

clues.name: Yellowstripe Goatfish
clues.fact: In Hawaii it's called the 'nightmare weke,' since eating it, especially the head, is said to bring nightmares or hallucinations.

clues.name: Hidden Hermit Crab
clues.fact: Olive green with dark-tipped legs and a bigger left claw, it often loses out to a close relative when competing for shells.

rounds.name: Tongariro National Park
rounds.official: Tongariro National Park World Heritage Site, NZ

clues.name: Common Chaffinch
clues.fact: After farmers thresh their crops, it sometimes spends weeks picking grain out of the discarded chaff, which likely gave it its name.

clues.name: common heather
clues.fact: Its nectar contains callunene, which makes a common bumble bee parasite lose its flagellum and become less infectious.

clues.name: Kelp Gull
clues.fact: Adults have black upperparts and wings, a yellow bill with a red spot, and greenish-yellow legs that brighten when breeding.

clues.name: Blue Duck
clues.fact: The male's high-pitched whistle gave it the Māori name whio, and it's pictured on the back of New Zealand's $10 note.

clues.name: New Zealand Red Admiral
clues.fact: Its Māori name, kahukura, means 'red cloak,' and its caterpillars feed on stinging nettles, especially ongaonga.

clues.name: Maui's copper
clues.fact: Found only in New Zealand, its caterpillars feed on Muehlenbeckia, and adults fly from October to April.

clues.name: Canada Goose
clues.fact: A common park bird, it's often called a pest for its droppings, noise, aggression and habit of stalking and begging for food.

clues.name: Great Crested Grebe
clues.fact: Pairs court each other with elaborate, synchronized dances, showing off striking black, orange-brown and white plumage.

clues.name: Tūī
clues.fact: Looking black at first glance with a white tuft at its neck, it resembles a parson, and early colonists called it the parson bird.

clues.name: Long-nosed Fur Seal
clues.fact: It dives deeper and longer than any other fur seal, with males reaching about 380 meters for around 15 minutes.

clues.name: Common Forest Looper
clues.fact: Endemic to New Zealand, it turned up in a garden light trap in west Cornwall in 2007, the first record outside New Zealand.

clues.name: Lacebark Looper
clues.fact: Its caterpillar has a white stripe down its back that looks like a leaf vein, camouflaging it on some of its host plants.
